name: Wadi Musa Town Centre
tagline: Central hub above the Petra gate
description: The town centre of Wadi Musa, around the Shaheed roundabout, holds most restaurants, shops, ATMs, bakeries and mid-range hotels. Set on the hills above the Petra visitor entrance, it is the main hub for supplies, dining and onward transport.
bestFor: Travellers wanting restaurants, shops and services in one walkable hub

name: Lower Wadi Musa (Near Petra Gate)
tagline: Closest area to the Petra entrance
description: The lower end of Wadi Musa sits closest to the Petra visitor centre and main gate, clustered with hotels, souvenir shops and eateries. Staying here means the shortest walk to the Siq each morning, ideal for early or repeat visits to the site.
bestFor: Visitors wanting the shortest walk to Petra's entrance each day

name: Upper Wadi Musa (Ain Musa area)
description: Upper Wadi Musa, near the Ain Musa (Moses Spring) area at the top of town, offers budget hotels and guesthouses with sweeping valley views. It is farther from the Petra gate but quieter and cheaper, with local shops and easier vehicle access.
bestFor: Budget travellers wanting valley views and quieter hilltop lodging

name: Gaia (Wadi Musa Village)
description: Gaia is the older traditional village neighbourhood on the eastern side of Wadi Musa, more residential than the tourist strip. It offers a glimpse of local Jordanian life, small shops and guesthouses, with a calmer atmosphere away from the main hotel zone.
bestFor: Travellers wanting local village life away from the tourist strip
